Kazakhstan is now visa free for Indians.

If you have been seeing Almaty everywhere lately, in reels, in office chats, in family WhatsApp groups, here is why. As of 2025, Indian passport holders can enter Kazakhstan without applying for any visa at all, for stays up to 14 days.

This has made Almaty one of the fastest growing destinations for Indian travelers heading into 2026. Mountains, dramatic canyons, modern cafes and a short flight from India, it genuinely feels like a different world without the usual visa hassle.

Four to six days is enough to cover the highlights, from Shymbulak in the mountains to Charyn Canyon and the cafe culture around the city center.

We do not believe in fixed, one size fits all itineraries. Every Almaty trip we plan is built around how you actually want to travel.

Curious what an Almaty holiday built around you could look like?

Dream it. Plan it. Explore it.

Andaman in 2026: more than just another beach trip

Planning Andaman this year? Most travelers ask the same things. How many days do you really need. What is the best season. Which islands actually matter.

Here is what years of planning these trips has taught us. Five nights and six days covering Port Blair, Havelock and Neil Island gives you the right balance, enough time to enjoy Radhanagar Beach without rushing between ferries.

We do not believe in fixed, one size fits all itineraries. A honeymoon couple needs a different pace from a family travelling with kids and elders, so every Andaman trip we plan is built around how you actually want to travel.

Curious what an Andaman holiday built around you could look like?

Dream it. Plan it. Explore it.

Women Only Group Tours

She did not want to wait for someone to travel with. So she booked a seat on a trip designed entirely for her.

More women across Mumbai are choosing to travel on their own terms in 2026, and women only group tours are becoming the easiest, safest way to do exactly that.

These trips include same gender room sharing, so no one pays extra to travel alone, thoughtfully chosen accommodation, and itineraries paced for comfort rather than rushed.

We think about the small details that often get missed elsewhere. Hotel locations that feel safe to step out of in the evening. Local guides who are respectful and reliable. Group sizes that are thoughtful, not too large to feel impersonal, not too small to feel awkward.

If you have been waiting for the right companion or the right moment, this might be the sign you needed. You do not need a reason beyond simply wanting to go.

Dream it. Plan it. Explore it.

Tier 2 Cities, Tier 1 Dreams

More direct flights. More disposable income. More dreams taking off, and not just from Mumbai or Delhi anymore.

Some of the fastest growth in Indian travel today is coming from cities like Indore, Surat, Nagpur, Coimbatore, and Lucknow.

Here's the interesting part. Even as more people from these cities plan international trips, many still prefer working with an experienced Mumbai based travel partner. Mumbai has long been a hub for visa processing, embassy coordination, and international flight connections, and that experience translates into smoother planning, no matter where the traveller actually lives.

A family from Nagpur planning a Switzerland honeymoon gets the same level of personalized planning as someone walking into our Mumbai office, just coordinated entirely over phone and WhatsApp.

You do not need to be based in a metro city to get expert level holiday planning anymore. What matters is working with a partner who has handled enough visas and itineraries to know where small mistakes usually happen, before they happen to you.

A good trip is built the same way, no matter where you are calling from.

Dream it. Plan it. Explore it.

Why a 4.8 Rating Across 100+ Reviews Actually Means Something

Anyone can put five stars on a website. Screenshots get edited, reviews get bought, one glowing testimonial proves very little on its own.

What is harder to fake is a rating built from over 100 real travellers, across different trips, different budgets, still holding steady at 4.8.

A single review only tells you about one person's one trip. But when more than a hundred people, across honeymoons, family vacations, and group tours, land in roughly the same place, that is not luck. That is a pattern.

A 4.8 is not a perfect 5, and that gap matters. Real travel involves real variables, flight delays, a hotel room not exactly as pictured. A 4.8 means almost everyone had a genuinely good experience, while leaving room for the small, honest hiccups that happen in real travel.

That is what consistency looks like, and consistency is what you are actually paying for when you book a trip.

We hold ourselves to that standard, trip after trip, traveller after traveller.

Dream it. Plan it. Explore it.

25 Years, One Promise

25 years ago, planning a trip meant trusting a travel agent you had never met. Today it means apps, chatbots, and a hundred websites promising the lowest price.

We have lived through both worlds. And here is what we learned: the tools change every few years. What a traveller actually needs almost never does.

People still want to feel certain, not just informed. Reading twenty reviews about a hotel is not the same as someone who has actually sent travellers there telling you honestly if it fits your family.

People still want someone to call when something goes wrong. A booking app cannot answer at midnight when your flight gets cancelled in a country you have never visited. A real travel consultant can.

This is exactly why, even in 2026, more travellers are choosing real planning support over guessing alone with too many online options.

That is the promise that has not changed for us in over 25 years and 1,000+ travellers. The tools evolve. What stays the same is understanding what you actually want from your trip, and building it around that.

Planning your next holiday? Message us through the contact options on this profile, no pressure, just honest guidance.

Dream it, Plan it. Explore it

WHY THE RIGHT ITINERARY MATTERS MORE THAN THE RIGHT HOTEL

Many travellers spend weeks choosing a hotel.

Comparing reviews.

Looking at photographs.

Checking facilities.

The itinerary.
